source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); Schedule S line A14 (ip25 PDF page 21), instructions PDF page 12 'Retirement benefits specifically exempt from Kansas Income Tax' (Thrift Savings Plans are the only employer plan named); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = employer plan distribution (you) 50,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 (15,750.00) = 34,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 50,000.00 + (0.00) = 50,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (single) 3,605.00; line 5 exemption allowance (1 exemption) 9,160.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 3,605.00 + 9,160.00 = 12,765.00; line 7 taxable income = 50,000.00 - 12,765.00 = 37,235.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 23,000.00 = 1,196.00 + 5.58% x (37,235.00 - 23,000.00 = 14,235.00) = 794.3130; total 1,990.3130 = 1,990.31. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 37,201-37,250, single, head of household or married filing separate column, PDF page 29, gives 1,990; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 1,990.31. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 1,990.31. A private 401(k): no line subtracts it. Were it a federal Thrift Savings Plan, line A14 would subtract it, but the inputs and projection cannot tell the two apart and the projection taxes both.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Thrift Savings Plan distributions, KPERS rollover withdrawals and Regents annuities are taxed (not_modelled).
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
